prattling.meaning: Talking in a way like a child, about small things.

inveterate.meaning: Fixed in a way of acting or feeling for a long time and not likely to change.

metaphysics.meaning: The study of very deep questions about life, mind and God.

ominous.meaning: Showing that something bad will happen.

evasions.meaning: Clever ways of getting out of doing something.

grovellers.meaning: People who lie face down on the floor.

sonorous.meaning: Having a deep, full, nice sound.

bankrupt.meaning: Having no money left. Here it is a joke about having nothing to give.

socratic.meaning: Using questions and answers to teach, as the Greek thinker Socrates did.

paragraphs.context: I cannot feel that I have done my duty as humble historian of the March family
paragraphs.mainIdea: The writer says Daisy and Demi, the twins, are so adored that they are almost spoilt, and praises how early they could do things.
paragraphs.simple: The writer says she has not done her duty as the humble historian of the March family unless she gives at least one chapter to its two most precious and important members. Daisy and Demi had reached the age when they could think for themselves. In this fast age, babies of three or four claim their rights, and they get them, which is more than many older people do. If ever there was a pair of twins in danger of being utterly spoilt by love, it was these chattering Brookes. Of course they were the most remarkable children ever born. They walked at eight months and talked well at twelve months. At two years they took their places at table and behaved so well that all who saw them were charmed.

paragraphs.context: Demi, like a true Yankee, was of an inquiring turn, wanting to know everything
paragraphs.mainIdea: Demi always wants to know the reason for everything. He also likes deep thoughts, and his grandfather talks with him like a teacher.
paragraphs.simple: Demi, like a true Yankee, liked to ask questions and wanted to know everything. He often got upset because he could not get answers that satisfied him to his endless 'What for?' He also liked deep thinking, which delighted his grandfather. His grandfather used to have Socratic talks with him. In these the clever pupil sometimes puzzled his teacher, to the open pleasure of the women of the family.

sentences.context: for honesty is the best policy in love as in law
sentences.simple: Being honest is the best way in love, as it is in law.
sentences.grammar: 'Honesty is the best policy' is a well-known saying. The pattern 'as in' adds a second area where the same is true.

sentences.context: If the boy had replied like Alcibiades, “By the gods, Socrates, I cannot tell,” his grandfather would not have been surprised
sentences.simple: If Demi had answered like Alcibiades, 'By the gods, Socrates, I cannot tell', his grandfather would not have been surprised.
sentences.grammar: This is an unreal 'if' sentence about the past: 'if ... had replied ... would not have been'. It compares Demi to a student in an old Greek story.

sentences.context: Mr. Bhaer’s devotion was sincere, however likewise effective
sentences.simple: Mr. Bhaer's love for children was true, and it also worked well.
sentences.grammar: 'However' here means 'in whatever way', or 'but also'. The word 'likewise' adds a second good point about his devotion.

turn topsy-turvy.meaning: To put things into a state of mess and disorder.
